relevance_note: Single-patient case report of a man with LAD1 and a stated ITGB2 genotype: 'A 19-year-old man with LAD1 (homozygous for ITGB2 c.IVS15–2A→G; p.D750_K755)'.
method_note: Hand extraction from the text; output assembled with a short Python script whose values were all typed from my reading, and every span was checked verbatim against the paper. No tables in the paper; the supplementary appendix (Fig. S1) is not included in the Markdown. Scope: the case patient ('patient', rule 5) plus 'unnamed person 1', the 'another patient with LAD1' whose resected sacral tissue was examined; included because the paper gives an individual-level fact (resected inflamed sacral tissue with IL-17-producing T cells); no sex, age or variant given for that person. The 'other patients with LAD1' in Fig. 1C/D are a group without individual detail and get no rows. Age at last evaluation is the age at presentation ('19-year-old'); follow-up continued for more than 1 year (to 14 months) but no later age is stated. Age at onset left not reported: delayed umbilical cord separation implies the neonatal period but no age is written; infections are dated 'early childhood' (recorded as feature onset). 'Otitis' (not specified as otitis media) left the checklist item 'otitis media' not reported. The sacral wound is not called necrotic or an ulcer, so 'necrotic skin ulcers or pyoderma gangrenosum-like lesions' is not reported; it is recorded under 'impaired wound healing' as a nonhealing wound. 'without progression of bone resorption or tooth loss' during treatment does not state whether teeth were lost before, so tooth loss is not reported. Appendicitis was not mapped to 'colitis or gastrointestinal inflammatory disease'. Fever excluded only from 'On admission, the patient was afebrile' (point in time). Variant type not stated by the authors (not derived from the IVS notation); no parental testing, pathogenicity or transcript stated. cites_prior_report_of_same_patients left null: the paper refers to earlier work on LAD1 patients but does not say this patient was described before. No contradictions found.
